idiom_name: Laminar/Airstream: state in Var and Signal values, component functions as pure Modifier builders
implementation_notes: In Laminar the container is whatever owns the reactive state - a Var or Signal held by a parent - and the children are ordinary functions that build elements from the values and signals they are handed. There is no virtual DOM and no component instances, so a child is literally a pure function of its inputs (for example `def textInput(mods: Modifier[Input]*): HtmlElement`), which makes the stateless role the default. Pass signals into children rather than plain values when the child must update (`value <-- query`, `onInput --> query`), and keep all mutation in the owner. Server-rendered Scala uses the same split with a Play action plus a Twirl template that receives explicit parameters.
pitfalls: Holding reactive state outside the owning component (a global Var, or a val captured beyond its lifetime) makes ownership invisible and leaks subscriptions; create and dispose state with its owner.
A two-way sink such as `onInput --> query` combined with a parent that also writes the same Var can loop; pick one writer per interaction path.
Rendering dynamic children without a keyed or split strategy re-creates elements on every emission and loses focus and scroll position.
